description: One hand over the shoulder, one up the back, and measure the gap. Your behind-back reach is a combined report on your shoulder tendons, capsule, and thoracic spine. Here is the zero-gap line, why the cuff heals slowly, and the wall work that closes the distance.

scenes.narration: Stand tall and take your right hand up and over your shoulder, reaching down the middle of your back, palm against your spine. Now take your left hand behind you from below and climb it up your back, knuckles against your spine, reaching for the first hand. How close do the fingertips get? Can they touch? Overlap? Or is there a gap you could park a fist inside? Estimate the distance in centimetres, then swap arms and do the other side, because they will not match. That gap is your Shoulder Reach Test, and it is sneakily complete: it visits the rotator cuff, the joint capsule, the chest, and the upper back in a single ten-second movement. Most people have never measured it once in their lives, which is why shoulder range vanishes so quietly. Remember your worse side and its gap. At the end, I grade it.

lines: A big gap is a flag.
beats.title: COMPARE THE SIDES

scenes.label: FINGERTIPS THAT MEET BEHIND YOU
scenes.narration: Here is the line. Fingertips that TOUCH or overlap behind your back mean the whole shoulder complex still owns its range. A gap under ten centimetres is the common modern pattern: a stiffening system that still moves well enough to ignore, which is precisely when it is cheapest to fix. Beyond twenty centimetres, or one side dramatically worse than the other, the shoulder is telling you its tendons, capsule, and upper back have been negotiating a smaller and smaller world for years. Two honest qualifiers. Shoulder shape varies, so your grade is against your own other side and your own history, not against a gymnast. And a gap that shrinks month by month is healing, whatever its absolute size. This test is a monthly photograph, not a daily judgement.
scenes.sub: touching: full range - under 10 cm: stiffening - 20+: stiff system

scenes.narration: Your shoulder is the most mobile joint you own and the least stable, a golf ball balanced on a tee. What keeps the ball centred while your arm moves is the ROTATOR CUFF, four muscles and their tendons wrapping the joint, constantly making small corrections you never feel. The reach test grades that whole arrangement at once. The top hand needs the cuff and the back of the capsule to lengthen. The bottom hand needs internal rotation, chest length, and an upper back that can extend. A shrinking gap can come from any of them, which is why shoulder healing is rarely one exercise. It is a system being re-taught its full map. And like every tendon story in this season, the cuff tendons live on a modest blood supply, especially near their attachment, so their repairs are scheduled in months. Slow tissue, system problem, patient fix.

beats.text: PAIN UP HIGH, STIFF DOWN LOW

lines: Joints need visits to stay open.
beats.title: WHY BOTH MATTER

scenes.narration: Here is why shoulders confuse people. Two different problems share one address. Tendon problems announce themselves as pain, often a specific arc of movement that hurts. Capsule and mobility problems announce themselves as stiffness, range that simply is not there, pain or not. Treat stiffness with strengthening alone and the gap barely moves. Treat a tendon like a stretching problem and you can irritate it for months. The reach test helps you separate them: pain with decent range points one way, painless stiffness points the other, and many shoulders honestly have some of both. The plan that covers the real world combines them: gentle load for the cuff, so the tendons remodel, plus regular, relaxed visits to the end of range, so the capsule keeps the doors open. Strengthen, then reach, in that order, most days.

beats.text: THE UPPER BACK IS HALF THE TEST
FIX THE FRAME, NOT JUST THE JOINT

scenes.narration: Now the angle almost everyone misses: half of your reach result is not your shoulder at all. It is your THORACIC SPINE, the upper back the shoulder blades ride on. Years of rounded sitting park that spine in a curve, and a shoulder sitting on a rounded base starts every movement already behind. Reaching down your back demands the upper back extend; reaching up it demands the chest open and the shoulder blade rotate. This is why two people with identical shoulders can score ten centimetres apart. The frame decides. So the healing plan includes the frame: wall slides that glide the blades upward, chest openers in doorways, and sitting tall often enough that tall becomes normal. Fix the frame and the joint suddenly looks healthier, because it finally gets to start from its real home position.

Your advantage here is obvious the moment you try the test. The reach grades how freely a light arm travels through positions, and your arms are light, unencumbered by the mass that makes big shoulders mechanically crowded. Bulky athletes lose this test to their own muscle; there is simply more of them in the way. You have no such excuse and no such obstacle. Your cuff work needs nothing heavier than a bottle of water, your range work needs a wall and a doorway, and your upper back can be retrained at bodyweight. Mobility is the one physical quality where being built light is a straight, unfair head start. The guys with the impressive shoulders envy the grade you can reach in a season of small daily work. Quietly take it.
Now open it with me. Back and arms on the wall, slide up slow, ribs down, no arching. Forty seconds on, twenty off, three rounds. Smooth and tall. Go.

beats.text: CAN'T LIFT THE ARM = GET SEEN

scenes.narration: Your week is a two-part habit. Wall slides or similar blade work most days, plus thirty relaxed seconds of the reach itself, towel in hand if the gap is wide, letting the top hand gently assist. Never force the bottom hand upward; the capsule opens for patience, not for violence. The mistakes that keep shoulders stiff: training only the comfortable side, which widens the gap that actually predicts trouble. Stretching cold, hard, and once a week. And blaming the cuff for what the upper back is doing. The honest line, and shoulders deserve it early: a shoulder that locks up fast over a few weeks, one you cannot lift after an injury, night pain that will not settle, or a gap that keeps growing despite the work, see a professional if it persists. Frozen shoulders and torn cuffs are real, and they reward early professional eyes.

scenes.label: THEN WE MEASURE THE GAP AGAIN
scenes.narration: So, your grade. A gap over twenty centimetres, or one side far worse, means system work: frame, capsule, and cuff together, with the worse side getting the attention until the sides reconcile. Under ten centimetres is the stiffening grade, the cheapest problem in this whole season to fix, because the tissue still remembers the range. Fingertips touching means a full map; maintain it with the daily habit and spend your ambition elsewhere. Watch the gap the way you would watch a bank balance: monthly, honestly, without drama. Shrinking is healing, whatever the starting number was. Put your gap in the comments. Just the number. We measure it again in thirty days.
scenes.sub: 20+ cm: system work - under 10: stiffening - touching: full range
